title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: Frobenius-class rho with a cyclotomic-squaring branch

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in proof.md (compute g=e(P0,Q); solve z=g^x by parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT with R=1024 twisted multipliers, a 4-Fp-multiplication canonical-conjugate key, a Granger-Scott cyclotomic-squaring branch taken with probability 3/8 (branch, multiplier and distinguished-point bits read from the class key K), deterministic fruitless-cycle escapes, and hard caps on steps, reports, restarts, false-fingerprint verifications and a metered total-work abort at 2^125.80 whose firing probability (Hoeffding, below exp(-2^117)) is part of the failure budget; output P=[x]P0 and verify e(P,Q)=z) succeeds with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^125.80 total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents (C=20,000), including setup, pairings, table construction, walk starts, distinguished-point handling, cycle handling, detection delay, output and verification. The table multiply is the reference operation (1 unit); the squaring branch is priced at 11,400 scalar instructions (0.57 unit) and every step carries 2,500 instructions of key and bookkeeping work. Peak memory is below 2^73 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^31 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound relies on the standard random-mapping heuristic for rho walks, adjusted for the branch mix (effective class count N/(1-s^2-(1-s)^2/R)), with model success 0.43 against the required 0.39, supported by toy-field experiments and by running the production step rule in the real BLS12-381 GT; no production-size run is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Part A: on real BLS12-381 GT elements check the Frobenius formula, the 4-multiplication conjugate-key formula, distinctness of the 12 keys, the canonical representative, the Granger-Scott squaring formula with its operation counts (9 Fp2 squarings, 34 Fp2 additions), the factorisation of r-1 and the orders of p and 2 modulo r. Part C: execute the production step rule (branch, multiplier and distinguished bits read from K, twisted table, squaring, 2-cycle escape) in the real GT for thousands of steps and compare against explicit Frobenius arithmetic. Part B: run the complete algorithm (cycle escapes, distinguished points, collision solving) in a small field with the same tower shape and compare first-collision times with the random-mapping law adjusted for the branch mix. Part E: sample classes, apply one step and count image coincidences to test the pair-collision law of the branch mix. Part D: recompute the work ledger. Toy scale only; does not validate production costs.
